originalGoal: Add a consistent retry policy to the TypeScript and Python SDKs. Specify retryable HTTP statuses (429 and 503), Retry-After handling, exponential backoff, maximum attempts and non-idempotent request protection in a new contracts/retry-policy.md before implementation. Implement and unit-test that contract in clients/typescript/client.ts and clients/python/client.py. Review both clients together and write reproducible conformance scenarios and results in tests/sdk-conformance.md, checking both use identical policy semantics. If that review finds nonconformance, request corrections to both client implementations and repeat the conformance review. Do not put retry behavior in the server or browser app.

nodes.name: retry_policy_contract
nodes.task: Create contracts/retry-policy.md in the Atlas workspace as the single authoritative retry specification that both SDK clients (clients/typescript/client.ts, clients/python/client.py) must implement identically. The contract must unambiguously specify, with concrete defaults and worked examples: (1) retryable HTTP statuses — exactly 429 and 503; (2) Retry-After handling — honor the header when present and parseable for a retryable response, covering both delta-seconds and HTTP-date forms, including bounds and fallback to backoff when absent or invalid; (3) exponential backoff — the growth formula, base delay, cap, and whether jitter is allowed and how it must be bounded so both SDKs can be tested deterministically; (4) maximum attempts — define the attempt-counting semantics and reconcile with the pre-existing project default documented in docs/configuration.md and src/settings.ts ("retryCount is the maximum number of retries; default 3") so it is explicit whether the default means 3 retries or 4 total attempts, and how a caller overrides it; (5) non-idempotent request protection — exactly which request forms are retried by default and how a caller may opt in to retrying others; (6) explicit scope boundary: retry lives only in the two SDK clients, never in server/ or web/. Do NOT implement any client code and do NOT modify server/, web/, src/, or docs/. Keep the file structured (per-requirement sections with normative MUST/SHOULD language) so an independent conformance reviewer can later check each requirement one by one.

nodes.name: typescript_client_retry
nodes.task: Implement the retry policy defined in contracts/retry-policy.md (authoritative; read it first) inside clients/typescript/client.ts in the Atlas workspace, replacing the current stub `export class Client { constructor(public baseUrl: string) {} }`. The client must perform HTTP requests with: retry only on the contract's retryable statuses (429 and 503), Retry-After handling per the contract's parsing rules, the contract's exponential backoff formula with deterministic seams so tests can pin delays/jitter, the contract's maximum-attempts semantics and caller override, and the contract's non-idempotent request protection defaults and opt-in. Add unit tests exercising the contract's behavior (retryable vs non-retryable statuses, Retry-After seconds and HTTP-date and invalid/absent cases, backoff sequence, attempt cap exhaustion, non-idempotent requests not retried by default and retried when opted in) using the repository's existing harness: package.json declares "type": "module" with a `node --test` test script, and other tests live under tests/ (e.g. tests/normalize.test.ts). Tests must not require a live server or network. Do not modify contracts/retry-policy.md semantics, the Python client, server/, or web/. Keep existing public constructor behavior (baseUrl) unless the contract requires otherwise. Verify by running the node --test suite for the TypeScript client and confirming all tests pass.

nodes.name: python_client_retry
nodes.task: Implement the retry policy defined in contracts/retry-policy.md (authoritative; read it first) inside clients/python/client.py in the Atlas workspace, replacing the current stub `class Client: def __init__(self, base_url)`. Semantics must match the contract exactly and therefore be identical to the TypeScript client: retry only on 429 and 503, Retry-After handling per the contract's parsing rules (delta-seconds and HTTP-date, fallback when absent/invalid), the contract's exponential backoff formula with deterministic seams so tests can pin delays/jitter, the contract's maximum-attempts semantics and caller override, and non-idempotent request protection defaults plus opt-in. Add unit tests covering the same behaviors as listed in the contract; place them under clients/python/ or tests/ using an approach that runs with the available Python interpreter and stdlib (no third-party HTTP server or network required — inject a fake transport). The repository's package.json test script covers only TypeScript; state clearly in your report how the Python tests are invoked (exact command). Do not modify contracts/retry-policy.md semantics, the TypeScript client, server/, or web/. Keep existing public constructor behavior (base_url). Verify by running the Python unit tests and confirming they pass.

nodes.name: sdk_conformance_review
nodes.task: Independently review the two SDK retry implementations against contracts/retry-policy.md and write the results into tests/sdk-conformance.md in the Atlas workspace, overwriting its placeholder text ("No retry contract is defined yet."). Inputs: contracts/retry-policy.md, clients/typescript/client.ts with its node --test unit tests, clients/python/client.py with its unit tests and the documented invocation command. Work: (1) For every requirement in the contract (retryable statuses 429/503, Retry-After delta-seconds and HTTP-date parsing plus absent/invalid fallback, exponential backoff formula/cap/jitter bounds, maximum-attempts semantics and the retryCount default reconciliation, non-idempotent protection and opt-in), record a reproducible conformance scenario: the concrete setup (request sequence, statuses, headers), the expected behavior per the contract, the exact command to reproduce it against each client, and the observed actual result and PASS/FAIL for BOTH clients side by side, with a clear identical-semantics verdict per requirement. Prefer deterministic reproduction (fake transports / injected clocks) over live servers. (2) Re-run both unit-test suites and record exit codes and pass counts. (3) Confirm the scope boundary: retry behavior exists only in the two SDK clients, and server/, web/, and src/ contain no retry implementation (note: src/settings.ts retryCount default 3 and server/config.ts, web/config.ts referencing it are pre-existing configuration, not SDK retry behavior). Do not modify any implementation code or the contract. End your reply with exactly one verdict on the final line: <ACCEPT> if every contract requirement conforms in both clients with identical semantics and the scope boundary holds; <REVISE> otherwise, and before that final line list each nonconformance with the file, the contract requirement violated, and the concrete correction requested.
